methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $1.7B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Atoms is a Growth-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Travis Kalanick that has raised $1.7B to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises nine peers (one public, eight private), including companies such as Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tier characteristics to support a reliable peer-median approach; only one public reference point exists in the sector.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on a stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($1.7B) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Growth-stage progression, the implied valuation is $2.0B. This method is most applicable in contexts where recent fundraising reflects current fair value and stage-based multiples are empirically grounded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B (floor, using raised capital) to $2.3B (ceiling, derived from upside case on the 1.2x multiplier). The median point is $2.0B. Critical uncertainties include the absence of tightly comparable Growth-stage robotics companies with disclosed valuations, limiting ability to anchor against market precedent. Revenue multiples, cash position, and burn rate would refine this range materially but are not available in the current dataset.
